nodes.title: Non-vanishing on hyperplanes
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field, m,N≥2, d_h positive integers, 0<Θ≤1, and d_h/d_(h+1)≥2m²/Θ. Let F∈K[X_hl] be nonzero and multihomogeneous of block degrees d_h. Let b_h∈K^N be nonzero and V_h={x:b_h·x=0}. Suppose H₂(b_h)^{d_h}≥(exp(Σd_h)H₂(coeff F))^{(N−1)(3m²/Θ)^m} for each h. Then there are x_h∈V_h and a Hasse multiindex i with w_d(i)=Σ_hΣ_l i_hl/d_h<mΘ and (D^iF)(x)≠0. The points and the derivative are K-rational.
proofSteps: Choose a nonzero pivot p_h of b_h and use large-height-binary-direction to choose q_h≠p_h. Permute each block so these are its first two coordinates. The coefficient height is unchanged by the support bijection and height2-zero-extension; block degrees and weighted orders are unchanged because the permutation stays within each block. Transport Hasse jets using their monomial coefficient formula.

Write the reordered polynomial using E=Fin(m)×Fin(N−2) extra variables and B=Fin(m)×Fin(2) binary variables. Put x*_h=(b_(h,1),−b_(h,0)). Its height to the power N−1 bounds H₂(b_h), it is nonzero, and it satisfies the binary hyperplane equation.

For the contradiction assume every jet of weight <mΘ vanishes on the product of hyperplanes. For arbitrary extra coordinates u, keep the second binary coordinate x*_(h,1) fixed and replace the first by x*_(h,0)−Σ_a b_(h,a+2)u_(h,a)/b_(h,0). This affine substitution lies in the hyperplanes. Apply binary-slice-vanishing with J={binary i:w_d(i)<mΘ}. Obtain one nonzero coefficient slice P=Q_e whose every such jet vanishes at x*.

Put s_h=Σ_a e_(h,a). binary-slice-block-degrees gives s_h≤d_h and degrees d_h−s_h. Multiply P by ∏_h X_(h,0)^{s_h}. restore-binary-multihomogeneity gives a nonzero F* of degrees d_h. height2-coefficient-slice and height2-monomial-multiplication give H₂(coeff F*)≤H₂(coeff F).

The strict-threshold vanishing characterization gives index(P,x*,d)≥mΘ. The existing index product theorem and nonnegativity give index(F*,x*,d)≥index(P,x*,d). Equivalently, in the Hasse Leibniz sum every derivative of P has order bounded by the total derivative order, so all jets of F* of weight <mΘ vanish. No assumption that the multiplying monomial is nonzero at x* is needed.

Let A=(3m²/Θ)^m>0 and B=exp(Σd_h)H₂(coeff F)>0. The original hypothesis and pair bound imply B^{(N−1)A}≤H₂(x*_h)^{(N−1)d_h}. Taking the positive (N−1)-st root gives B^A≤H₂(x*_h)^{d_h}. Monotonicity and the coefficient-height bound give exactly sharp-roths-lemma for F*. Its nonzero jet of weight <mΘ contradicts the preceding vanishing. Convert its ordinary-derivative signature to Hasse derivatives with the existing factorial identity; characteristic zero makes the factors nonzero.

This is Evertse Lemma 24 reduced to the existing sharp-roths-lemma node. That node retains the explicit Faltings/Product Theorem proof gap; the reduction does not claim that gap is closed. For N=2 the extra-variable type is empty, e=0 and F*=F, giving the same argument without an extraction step.

nodes.title: A normal vector with the hyperplane height
nodes.statement: For a number field K, N≥2 and a submodule T≤K^N with dimension N−1, there is b∈K^N with b≠0, T=dotOrthogonal(K·b), and subspaceHeight(T)=H₂(b).
proofSteps: The submodule is proper by its dimension. The pinned separating-functional theorem supplies a nonzero linear functional f with T≤ker f. Its kernel has dimension N−1 by the dual rank lemma, so equality follows from inclusion and equal dimensions.
Put b_j=f(e_j). Expand any vector in the standard basis to get f(x)=Σ_j b_j x_j. Nonzero f implies b≠0. By bilinearity and commutativity, ker f is precisely dotOrthogonal(K·b).
Apply the existing subspaceHeight_orthogonal and subspaceHeight_span_singleton APIs. The latter uses N≥2 and b≠0.

nodes.title: A nonzero polynomial restriction in any hyperplane basis
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of hyperplane-nonvanishing, let a_(h,1),…,a_(h,N−1) be any basis of V_h. Then there is i with w_d(i)<mΘ such that (D^iF)(Σ_a Y_(1,a)a_(1,a),…,Σ_a Y_(m,a)a_(m,a)) is a nonzero polynomial. This is the precise input of conditional-nonzero-block-grid-jet.
proofSteps: Apply hyperplane-nonvanishing to obtain x_h∈V_h with a nonzero evaluated jet. Express each x_h in the supplied basis, using its spanning property; no height condition on the basis vectors is required.

Evaluate the composed polynomial at those basis coefficients. The pinned eval_eval₂ identity identifies its value with the nonzero original jet. Since the zero polynomial evaluates to zero, the composed polynomial is nonzero.

For a hyperplane given as a codimension-one submodule T rather than an equation, take a nonzero element b of its one-dimensional dot-orthogonal space. Then T=dotOrthogonal(K·b). The existing subspaceHeight_span_singleton and subspaceHeight_orthogonal give subspaceHeight(T)=H₂(b). Thus the parent grid theorem has exactly the required hypotheses.

api.statement: Under the hypotheses of hyperplane-nonvanishing, let a_(h,1),…,a_(h,N−1) be any basis of V_h. Then there is i with w_d(i)<mΘ such that (D^iF)(Σ_a Y_(1,a)a_(1,a),…,Σ_a Y_(m,a)a_(m,a)) is a nonzero polynomial. This is the precise input of conditional-nonzero-block-grid-jet.

acceptance: The basis can have arbitrary heights. Evaluation at a witness proves the restriction nonzero before the rectangular-grid lemma is invoked.

nodes.title: Block homogenization
nodes.statement: Let B and S be finite types, b:S→B assign each affine variable to a block, d:B→ℕ, and R be a commutative ring. Put t_h(e)=Σ_{j:b(j)=h}e_j and A_d(e)=(d_h−t_h(e))_h⊕e. Let H_d(f) denote blockHomogenize b d f. A polynomial is d-bounded when t_h(e)≤d_h for every e in its support and every h. Define H_d(f)=Σ_{e∈supp(f), ∀h t_h(e)≤d_h} coeff_e(f) X^{A_d(e)} in R[X_h0,Y_j], with variables B⊕S. The operation is total: it discards every monomial exceeding one of the block bounds. Under d-boundedness it is the usual product of X_h0^{d_h} times f(Y_j/X_b(j),0), expressed without localization.
proofSteps: Use the native coefficient support and finite sums, then the native monomial constructor at A_d(e). The inr coordinates recover e, so exponent padding introduces no collisions.
Filter before taking natural subtraction; saturation alone would retain overdegree terms and disagree with Polynomial.homogenize.
acceptance: Use block totals, native multivariate polynomials and Hasse derivatives; no characteristic-zero or nonzero-polynomial hypothesis is implicit.

nodes.title: Coefficients of block homogenization
nodes.statement: Let B and S be finite types, b:S→B assign each affine variable to a block, d:B→ℕ, and R be a commutative ring. Put t_h(e)=Σ_{j:b(j)=h}e_j and A_d(e)=(d_h−t_h(e))_h⊕e. Let H_d(f) denote blockHomogenize b d f. A polynomial is d-bounded when t_h(e)≤d_h for every e in its support and every h. For every exponent u on B⊕S, coeff_u(H_d(f)) equals coeff_{u|S}(f) if u(inl h)+t_h(u|S)=d_h for all h, and equals 0 otherwise. No degree bound on f is needed.
proofSteps: Expand the finite monomial sum and use coeff_monomial. At most one input exponent contributes, since its affine part must be u|S.
The condition on u is equivalent to admissibility of its affine restriction and equality of its homogenizing part to d−t(u|S); use natural subtraction only after establishing the inequality.
acceptance: Use block totals, native multivariate polynomials and Hasse derivatives; no characteristic-zero or nonzero-polynomial hypothesis is implicit.

nodes.title: Support bijection for block homogenization
nodes.statement: Let B and S be finite types, b:S→B assign each affine variable to a block, d:B→ℕ, and R be a commutative ring. Put t_h(e)=Σ_{j:b(j)=h}e_j and A_d(e)=(d_h−t_h(e))_h⊕e. If f is d-bounded, A_d is a bijection from supp(f) to supp(H_d(f)), preserving each coefficient. The declared theorem is the support bijection; coefficient preservation is supplied by the preceding coefficient node.
proofSteps: Apply the coefficient formula: a nonzero coefficient on either side corresponds to the unique affine restriction e.
A_d is injective by its inr coordinates. The support bound ensures every input coefficient survives. This remains a bijection of empty supports when f=0.

nodes.title: Dehomogenizing on the unit chart
nodes.statement: Let B and S be finite types, b:S→B assign each affine variable to a block, d:B→ℕ, and R be a commutative ring. Put t_h(e)=Σ_{j:b(j)=h}e_j and A_d(e)=(d_h−t_h(e))_h⊕e. If f is d-bounded, substituting X_h0=1 and retaining the affine variables in H_d(f) gives f as a polynomial over R.
proofSteps: Evaluate each monomial in the defining finite sum with aeval. All homogenizing factors become 1.
The degree hypothesis removes the filter; recover f from as_sum. This is a polynomial identity, with no inference from evaluation on a finite coefficient ring.

nodes.title: Agreement with univariate homogenization
nodes.statement: Let B and S be finite types, b:S→B assign each affine variable to a block, d:B→ℕ, and R be a commutative ring. Put t_h(e)=Σ_{j:b(j)=h}e_j and A_d(e)=(d_h−t_h(e))_h⊕e. Let H_d(f) denote blockHomogenize b d f. A polynomial is d-bounded when t_h(e)≤d_h for every e in its support and every h. For B=S=Unit and b=id, send an ordinary polynomial p to the one-variable multivariate polynomial using uniqueAlgEquiv⁻¹. Rename inl to 1 and inr to 0 in H_n(p); the result is the native Polynomial.homogenize p n for every p and n, including n below the degree of p.
proofSteps: Compare coefficients under the bijection sending the affine variable to native coordinate 0 and the homogenizing variable to native coordinate 1.

The block coefficient formula retains exactly the exponents u₀+u₁=n, and coeff_uniqueAlgEquiv_symm identifies the retained coefficient with p.coeff u₀. Polynomial.coeff_homogenize gives the same coefficient on the other side, also when n is below the degree of p. Finish by coefficient extensionality.

nodes.statement: Let B and S be finite types, b:S→B assign each affine variable to a block, d:B→ℕ, and R be a commutative ring. Put t_h(e)=Σ_{j:b(j)=h}e_j and A_d(e)=(d_h−t_h(e))_h⊕e. This holds for all f, since overdegree terms were filtered.

nodes.title: Reconstruction from an affine chart
nodes.statement: Let B and S be finite types, b:S→B assign each affine variable to a block, d:B→ℕ, and R be a commutative ring. Put t_h(e)=Σ_{j:b(j)=h}e_j and A_d(e)=(d_h−t_h(e))_h⊕e. Let H_d(f) denote blockHomogenize b d f. A polynomial is d-bounded when t_h(e)≤d_h for every e in its support and every h. If F on B⊕S is IsWeightedHomogeneous of degree d_h for every block indicator, then H_d(F(1,Y))=F.
proofSteps: For an exponent u with nonzero coefficient in F, homogeneity forces u(inl h)=d_h−t_h(u|S) and t_h(u|S)≤d_h.
Thus the affine restrictions of distinct surviving exponents are distinct. Dehomogenization neither collides nor cancels these coefficients, and all resulting exponents are d-bounded.
The coefficient formula for H_d reconstructs every coefficient of F.

nodes.title: Centered homogeneous Taylor expansion
nodes.statement: Let B and S be finite types, b:S→B assign each affine variable to a block, d:B→ℕ, and R be a commutative ring. Put t_h(e)=Σ_{j:b(j)=h}e_j and A_d(e)=(d_h−t_h(e))_h⊕e. Let H_d(f) denote blockHomogenize b d f. A polynomial is d-bounded when t_h(e)≤d_h for every e in its support and every h. Suppose f is d-bounded and a:S→R. Write Γ_d={γ:S→₀ℕ | ∀h t_h(γ)≤d_h}, a finite set (each γ_j≤d_b(j)). Then H_d(f)=Σ_{γ∈Γ_d} (D^γf)(a) ∏_h X_h0^{d_h−t_h(γ)} ∏_j(Y_j−a_j X_b(j),0)^{γ_j}, as a polynomial over R. D is the inherited Hasse derivative.
proofSteps: The inherited coefficient formula makes D^γf zero outside Γ_d: every coefficient would come from an exponent ν+γ whose block sum exceeds a bound.

Use the inherited Taylor formula in a polynomial coefficient ring, commuting Hasse derivatives with the coefficient map R→R[Y]. Set its center to the constants a and its increment to Y−a, to obtain a polynomial identity for f; pointwise equality over R alone is not used.

Native weighted homogeneity of X and C, followed by sub, mul, pow and sum, proves that every term and the whole displayed expression have degree d_h in block h. Substitution X_h0=1 gives the polynomial Taylor identity. Apply homogeneous reconstruction to this expression and the chart identity of H_d(f).

nodes.title: Triangular formula for homogeneous Hasse jets
nodes.statement: Let B and S be finite types, b:S→B assign each affine variable to a block, d:B→ℕ, and R be a commutative ring. Put t_h(e)=Σ_{j:b(j)=h}e_j and A_d(e)=(d_h−t_h(e))_h⊕e. Let H_d(f) denote blockHomogenize b d f. A polynomial is d-bounded when t_h(e)≤d_h for every e in its support and every h. Suppose f is d-bounded, a:S→R, κ:B→₀ℕ and β:S→₀ℕ. At q=(1,a), D^{κ⊕β}H_d(f)(q) equals the sum over γ∈Γ_d with β≤γ and t_h(γ−β)≤κ_h for every h of (D^γf)(a) times ∏_j binom(γ_j,β_j)(−a_j)^{γ_j−β_j} times ∏_h binom(d_h−t_h(γ), κ_h−t_h(γ−β)). Natural binomial coefficients are mapped to R. Every contributing γ has t_h(γ)≤κ_h+t_h(β).
proofSteps: In centered homogeneous Taylor, substitute X_h0=1+U_h and Y_j=a_j+V_j. The centered linear factors become V_j−a_j U_b(j).
For the coefficient of U^κV^β, choose V_j^{β_j} from each centered factor. This forces β≤γ and contributes binom(γ_j,β_j)(−a_j)^{γ_j−β_j}, together with U_h-exponent t_h(γ−β).

The remaining U_h exponent must be κ_h−t_h(γ−β); choosing it from (1+U_h)^{d_h−t_h(γ)} gives the last binomial. Terms with excessive forced U_h exponent contribute zero and must be excluded before subtraction.
Identify the translated coefficient with the Hasse jet by the inherited polynomial Taylor formula over a polynomial coefficient ring. The total-order inequality follows by summing γ=β+(γ−β).

nodes.title: Transport of strict jet thresholds
nodes.statement: Let B and S be finite types, b:S→B assign each affine variable to a block, d:B→ℕ, and R be a commutative ring. Put t_h(e)=Σ_{j:b(j)=h}e_j and A_d(e)=(d_h−t_h(e))_h⊕e. Let H_d(f) denote blockHomogenize b d f. A polynomial is d-bounded when t_h(e)≤d_h for every e in its support and every h. Assume every d_h>0, f is d-bounded, a:S→R, and T∈[0,∞]. Homogeneous Hasse jets of H_d(f) at (1,a) vanish for every order i of weight Σ_v i_v/d_block(v)<T if and only if affine Hasse jets of f at a vanish for every γ of weight Σ_j γ_j/d_b(j)<T. Each homogenizing variable has its block’s weight d_h.
proofSteps: For the forward implication use pure affine jets; adding zero homogenizing orders leaves the weight unchanged.
For the converse split i into κ⊕β and use the triangular formula. Each term has t_h(γ)≤κ_h+t_h(β), so its affine weight is no greater than the homogeneous weight and is strictly below T.
The affine vanishing premise kills every term. Positive d_h makes the finite-weight division and block regrouping valid. The argument also works for T=0 and T=∞ and for f=0.

nodes.title: Scaled divided derivative matrices
nodes.statement: For T ∈ ℂ[z], M ∈ M_n(ℂ[z]), define P₀=I and P_{m+1}=(T P′_m + P_m M − m T′ P_m)/(m+1). If T ≠ 0 and G=M/T, then P_m = T^m B_m where B_m is defined by y^{(m)}/m! = B_m y. This is a polynomial matrix recurrence; the derivative is entrywise.
hypotheses: Finite matrix index type; scalar field ℂ of characteristic zero. Algebraic coefficient assumptions are imposed by the arithmetic theorem that consumes the system.
proofSteps: Define P_m by recursion in polynomial matrices.
Induct on m in the rational function field: B₀=I, (m+1)B_{m+1}=B′_m+B_m G; differentiate P_m=T^m B_m and substitute. Every multiplication order is preserved.

nodes.title: Evaluation identifies a holomorphic linear-system solution space
nodes.statement: Under the positive-radius, holomorphic-coefficient hypotheses of Cauchy’s theorem, the ℂ-vector space of solutions on the disc D (restricted to D, or total representatives modulo equality on D) is linearly isomorphic to ℂⁿ by evaluation at z₀. Its dimension is n. No claim is made about the vector space of unrestricted total functions outside D.
hypotheses: r>0; coefficients holomorphic on the whole disc; the solution carrier identifies functions agreeing on D.
proofSteps: Define the solution space on D with pointwise addition and scalar multiplication.
Evaluation at z₀ is linear. Cauchy existence proves surjectivity and uniqueness on D proves injectivity.
The resulting linear equivalence transports the finite dimension n.
acceptance: The solutions of y′=y on a disc are represented by c·exp(z−z₀); evaluation returns c.
Changes outside D are identified, so they contribute no extra dimensions.

sources.match: The source’s n-dimensional local solution-space statement; whole-disc version follows from Cauchy existence and equality on D.

nodes.title: Cauchy initial jets for a scalar linear equation
nodes.statement: Let r>0, m≥1 and p₀,…,p_m be holomorphic on D={|z−z₀|<r}, with p_m nowhere zero on D. For every jet c₀,…,c_{m−1} there is a unique solution on D of Σ_{i=0}^m p_i y^{(i)}=0 with y^{(i)}(z₀)=c_i for i<m. Its solution space, restricted to D, has complex dimension m.
hypotheses: Positive-radius disc; holomorphic coefficients; positive order m; leading coefficient nonzero at every point of the disc.
proofSteps: Divide by p_m, whose reciprocal is holomorphic on D.
Form the m-dimensional companion system on (y, y′, …, y^(m−1)).
Use Cauchy’s initial-vector theorem and identify scalar solutions with companion-system solutions by the first coordinate; transport the evaluation equivalence.
acceptance: For y″=0, the unique solution with initial jet (c₀,c₁) is c₀+c₁(z−z₀).
For (z−1)y′=zy, a disc containing 1 fails the nowhere-zero leading-coefficient hypothesis.

sources.match: Companion-system equivalence and initial jets of the scalar Cauchy theorem.

nodes.title: Finite simplex discretisation for simultaneous inequalities
nodes.statement: For an integer q≥1 and a real 1/2≤γ<1, there is a finite set D of nonnegative vectors Γ∈ℝ^q with Σ_i Γ_i=γ such that, for every nonnegative vector y with Y=Σ_i y_i>0, some Γ∈D satisfies Γ_i Y≤y_i for all i. No explicit bound on the cardinality of D is asserted.
proofSteps: Choose a positive integer M≥q/(1−γ). Let G be the finite grid of q-tuples with coordinates k/M, 0≤k≤M. Retain its points f with Σ f≥γ and map them to Γ=γ f/(Σ f), giving the finite set D. Its vectors are nonnegative and have sum γ.
For a given y put f_i=⌊M y_i/Y⌋/M. Since 0≤y_i/Y≤1, this lies in G and f_i≤y_i/Y. The floor lower bound gives Σ f≥1−q/M≥γ, so it is retained.
Because γ/(Σ f)≤1, the resulting Γ_i≤f_i≤y_i/Y, giving Γ_i Y≤y_i.
acceptance: For q=1, D={γ} works since γ<1.
For γ=1 and q=2 no finite D works: domination of nonnegative vectors of sum 1 forces Γ=y, requiring the whole infinite simplex. The strict hypothesis γ<1 is necessary.

sources.match: The finite domination assertion; the reviewer supplies a direct floor-grid proof and does not assert the source’s sharper cardinality bound.

review.reason: The claim that equality is possible in the derivative bound is false for these auxiliary polynomials. Let m bound both degrees and W=P Q′−P′Q≠0. If the degrees differ, deg W≤deg P+deg Q−1≤2m−2; if both equal m, the leading degree-(2m−1) terms cancel, again giving deg W≤2m−2. For t the multiplicity of P−ξ₂Q at ξ₁, W is divisible by (X−ξ₁)^(t−1)f^(r−1), so t≤2m−d(r−1)−1<d(2εr+1). Hence a nonzero divided derivative of order k=t satisfies the printed strict bound. The source’s displayed Lemma 6.12 proof only states a weaker estimate; an omitted routine leading-coefficient sharpening is not a false strict result.

sourceIssues.printed: Lemma 2.2 asserts ∑_{w|v} log |x|_w = log |x|_v; Lemma 2.5 deduces invariance of h under field extension; Definition 2.7 then sets H(P) = H_K(P)^{1/[K:ℚ]}.
sourceIssues.correction: Choose one convention consistently. With Lemma 2.2’s degree-normalised local absolute values, Definition 2.4 is already the absolute logarithmic height, so Definition 2.7 should simply use H = exp h without a second degree root. Alternatively use relative local absolute values, replace the sum in Lemma 2.2 by [L:K] log |x|_v and Lemma 2.5 by h_L = [L:K] h_K; then Definition 2.7 is correct. The packet uses the latter convention for native Mathlib relative heights.
sourceIssues.reason: Let K = ℚ and L = ℚ(√2), and take P = [2:1]. Under Lemma 2.2, the sum of the archimedean logs over L is log 2 and the finite contributions to the height vanish, so Definition 2.4 gives H_L(P) = H_K(P) = 2 as Lemma 2.5 says. Definition 2.7 then gives 2 over K and √2 over L, contradicting its claimed independence. Under Mathlib’s relative convention H_L(P) = 4 and H_K(P) = 2, and the degree root restores equality.

restructure.detail: LD.6 builds Pila–Zannier-type unlikely-intersection results from 'independent orbit and functional-transcendence suppliers' and names Ax–Lindemann/Ax–Schanuel inputs. DT.5 proves the exponential (torus) case by Ax's differential-algebraic method (ax-schanuel-theorem, ax-lindemann-weierstrass). The modular and Shimura cases (Pila 2011; Pila–Tsimerman, arXiv:1412.8255) are proved with o-minimal counting and definable Chow, which LD.6 builds.
restructure.proposal: Add the stage link DiophantineApproximationAndTranscendence:DT.5 → LogicAndDefinabilityInNumberTheory:LD.6 (DT.5 supplies Ax–Schanuel and Ax–Lindemann–Weierstrass for the exponential); the j-function and Shimura-variety Ax–Lindemann/Ax–Schanuel theorems belong to LD.6. Unlikely-intersection theorems themselves stay with LD.6 (Pila–Zannier, André–Oort), HeightsRationalPointsAndObstructions:RP.5 (Mordell–Lang, Manin–Mumford, Bogomolov) and ArithmeticDynamics:DY.6; DT.5 plans none of them.

restructure.detail: Beukers' refinement of Siegel–Shidlovskii and the Mahler theory need the local theory of linear differential equations over ℂ(z) and Picard–Vessiot theory (differential Galois groups, identity components, the Galois correspondence); these are foundations used nowhere else in DT and planned by no roadmap.
restructure.proposal: A new roadmap 'Linear differential equations and differential Galois theory' with stages: (1) local solutions (the node DT.5/holomorphic-solutions-of-linear-systems moves there), regular singular points, Fuchs' criterion, apparent singularities; (2) Picard–Vessiot extensions and the differential Galois group as a linear algebraic group; (3) the Galois correspondence and identity components. DT.5 imports stages 1–3; FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration, which could have hosted them, is retired.

restructure.detail: The old absence claim is superseded by three freshly read pinned Tau Ceti declarations: injective integral extensions preserve Krull dimension; an injective integral map from a finite polynomial algebra computes dimension by the variable count; finite-type dimension is invariant under field extension. These are baseline inputs, not new nodes. What remains is their exact comparison with the fraction-field transcendence-degree interface and the torsion-free/flat finite-type family over the affine line used by fibre-dimension-over-the-affine-line and Siegel–Shidlovskii. Confirm the generic scheme/algebra owner before assigning new work; the inherited proposal must not re-plan the native integral-extension or field-base-change results.
restructure.proposal: Retain only the generic finite-type affine-family dimension/flatness comparison after importing the pinned Tau Ceti integral-extension and field-base-change theorems. Coordinate the exact remaining interface with SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.0; no scope amendment is applied in this pass.
